title: Unified usage delivery: fanout + manifest for CSV/S3 exports with idempotent retries
creator: Avery Chen
description: Replace and consolidate multiple ad-hoc delivery paths (scheduled CSV dumps, ad-hoc S3 uploads, and per-customer webhooks) with a single fanout service that emits immutable manifests and per-customer payload pointers. Goals: make exports idempotent and resumable, reduce duplicate compute for large tenants, provide a canonical audit record for billing and compliance, and enable efficient retention / backfill operations. The service should produce compact JSON manifest objects that reference CSV artifacts (S3 URIs) and delivery receipts (webhook statuses), support chunking for very large exports, and be compatible with existing customer subscription flows.
description_notes: Core components: export-generator (aggregates usage, shards into CSV blobs), delivery-fanout (creates manifest + kicks off per-destination workers), manifest-store (Dynamo/S3 manifest index), delivery-workers (S3 copy, signed URL creation, webhook POST with retries + dedupe), and backfill/orchestration. Must integrate with billing and console job dashboards for visibility.
comments: 2026-02-10 - Avery Chen: Initial proposal filed. Rationale: current system has 3 different delivery paths, inconsistent retry semantics, and no canonical manifest leading to duplicate exports and reconciliation pain between billing and customer reports. Proposed solution creates immutable manifests to drive downstream idempotency.

2026-02-15 - Riley Singh: Added delivery primitives design doc to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Unified+Usage+Delivery+Design. Called out S3 prefix layout tenant_id/year/month/day/export_id/part-N.csv and manifest.json next to the parts to aid cross-region replication and lifecycle rules.

2026-02-18 - Morgan Patel (PM): Asked for sampling strategy for customers producing >10M tokens/day. Decision: implement deterministic hash-based sampling that produces a stable subset per-export_id to allow consistent analytics and quota calculations.

2026-02-22 - Design review with Security: Agreed on client-side PII redaction hooks and KMS-encrypted S3 buckets for exports flagged as 'sensitive'. Security requested an audit log entry per manifest emission; added manifest-store writes to the critical path.

2026-02-28 - Engineering sync: Chose eventual consistency model for manifest-store but require manifest emission to be transactionally recorded (write-ahead) before fanout begins. Trade-off: slightly higher tail latency for export completion vs. much stronger recovery guarantees. Documented in design doc.

2026-03-03 - PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4217 implementing export-generator and manifest schema. PR includes unit tests for chunking logic and a simple local-file-backed manifest-store for dev. Requested reviewers @ekim and @jgarcia.

2026-03-05 - Code review comments (ekim): Add metrics for manifests_created_total, manifest_emission_latency_seconds, delivery_worker_retries_total, and per-tenant failed_delivery_rate. Also make sampling_rate an export-level parameter so PMs can tune for specific customers.

2026-03-08 - Integration test notes: Verified that manifest+parts flow through data-pipeline and are discoverable by the billing consumer. Observed duplicate webhook deliveries when a worker timed out and retried — added a dedupe header X-Redwood-Delivery-Id for idempotent webhook handling by customers, and server-side dedupe window of 24h indexed by delivery-id.

2026-03-10 - Ops: Ran a small internal canary for 5 customers for 48h. No data loss; one case of double-archive due to retries hitting a different region. Mitigation: use single-region canonical write for parts and cross-region replication via S3 replication configs rather than programmatic multi-region upload.

2026-03-12 - Riley Singh: Marked In Progress -> ready for larger QA. Next steps: add end-to-end smoke tests in staging, add customer-facing docs for new manifest format, and schedule a migration plan for existing scheduled CSV jobs to opt into manifests.

Outstanding tasks: update console job UI to show manifest IDs and per-destination delivery status; implement backfill coordinator to convert legacy dumps into manifests; add rate limits per-customer for fanout concurrency to control spend.
Follow-ups created: ENG-20590 (console UI manifest view), ENG-20612 (backfill coordinator), ENG-20631 (billing reconciliation consumer changes).
